title: Vie Towers
name: Ashley Kelly
text:
Please believe me when I say I’m looking in your best interest when I tell you to live and spend your money elsewhere.

One, the management here is so money hungry that I’d go as far to say they’re inhumane. They do not care about you as people and only want money. It’s like they generally cannot fathom being reasonable if it means they’re losing money, even when it’s clear as day that something isn’t fair. After your move out, they will charge you for damages you didn’t even create, no matter how small or trivial the “damages” are but yet will charge 10x more than what the damages equivalent to. Mind you, I already stated those damages upon move in, but since I didn’t note every single little detail of it, I am now liable? It’s so obvious that they charge residents for “damages” with no intentions of repairing said damage. They’re hoping that each new resident doesn’t make note of previous damages so they can charge them for those damages they didn’t even create a bank on that. Because if that wasn’t the case, I would’ve moved into a new unit with brand new and undamaged furniture and not been charged for an already old and damaged countertop. And since they charge for every small petty thing, every single unit should have repaired and replaced furniture after each resident leave, because the way they charge for things I doubt anyone can leave uncharged. After including myself, I’ve seen them charge other people I know for things that were inevitable and should be a part of the natural wear and tear law but they obviously don’t adhere to that. Since they’re charging everyone to replace/repair every small damages for the next resident, why isn’t anything new in any unit I’ve been in? Plus they’re so busy looking for small damages to bank on residence, they don’t even clean the units beforehand, I found clothes underneath my dresser that looked years old. Also, even if you notify them of the damages when you move in, no effort is made to repair/replace those damages and neither is there any compensation for making you live with those damage. The management and building is so unprofessional and shady, they’re not helpful nor accommodating in the slightest, so please don’t expect anything from them. Because they’re allowed to have so many issues with the building and the residents just had to deal with it, but the second a resident makes a slight mistake (mind you, not even my mistake) they have to drop hundreds of dollars?! And apparently, the insurance that Vie charges you monthly doesn’t even cover any damages??!

Second, there’s so many things wrong with the building. Please prepare yourself for many days with no hot water or the water going off completely, thermostat not working, elevator is not working, electricity going out and food getting spoiled for how long the electricity been out, Wi-Fi not working, package room losing your package with no intentions of helping on several different occasions, no one at the front desk half the times and no one picking up the phone or returning your calls of concern, machines being out of order in the gym, mold in units, and much more. I know all buildings might have their issues, but Vie Towers’ issues are quite excessive and truthfully not worth it. And I know plenty of surrounding nearby apartments that don’t even have half the amount of issues that Vie has.

Also, please know that mostly all their good reviews on here were because they baited residents into writing them for the chance to win a gift card. They know their management and building is so terrible that they wouldn’t get any good reviews otherwise. So please do not pay attention to the good reviews, especially the 5 stars as they’re all fabricated reviews that was only made due to luring their residents with gift cards.

If there’s any potential future residence reading this and thinking about signing a lease with them, please think about this very thoroughly and assess all your other options first, or expect to drop a pretty penny with moving out. Rent is too high for such low standards and living arrangements.

title: Vie Towers
name: C Cilius (CCrew19)
text:
I've lived here for approximately three years, and unfortunately, my overall experience was disappointing. To be clear, this review is not directed at the onsite staff. Hezzy, Shakaya, Mr. Oscar, and Mr. Will deserve their props for the work they do, and I am very much appreciative of them.

During my time here, residents experienced several major disruptions, including a week-long HVAC outage during the extreme heat of August 2024 and a water and electricity outage lasting more than three days in March 2025. In both situations, residents received little to no meaningful accommodation or consideration. The March outage, in particular, did not appear to receive serious attention until local media became involved.

After moving out, my electric bill tripled out of nowhere. Given the significant difference from my normal bills and the fact that my usage and appliances had not substantially changed, I expected management to take my concerns more seriously rather than simply dismissing them.

Overall, my experience left me feeling that communication, accountability, and resident concerns were not consistently treated with the importance they deserved. After three years, I expected better from management. Unfortunately, based on my experience, I cannot recommend this property.

title: Vie Towers

text:
⭐☆☆☆☆

Unfortunately, my experience with Vie Towers was extremely disappointing.

The biggest issue was the lack of responsiveness. I contacted the management team multiple times before my lease ended regarding my renter’s insurance and received little to no meaningful response. Had someone simply responded while I was still a tenant, I could have easily provided the requested documentation and resolved the matter. Instead, the issue was addressed only after my lease expired, resulting in charges that should never have been assessed.

Good customer service is about resolving issues while they can still be corrected, not waiting until after a resident moves out and then sending unexpected charges.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Vie Towers. I hope the management team improves its responsiveness and treats future residents with greater fairness and professionalism.

title: Vie Towers
name: Jevin Smith
text:
Genuinely, if a student needs housing, PLEASE find somewhere else to live. My first year in Vie was BEFORE the Howard partnership, and it was amazing. Everyone was kind, and everything worked. My second and third years, however, were very different. My second year we went without power and water for TWO AND A HALF DAYS. I lived on the top floor, and was unable to leave because the elevators were down and the stairwell was pitch black. I missed TWO DAYS of classes, and was unable to shower during that time. Once the elevators were operational, I had to go across the street to shower. The issue was resolved once the city deemed the building uninhabitable, and it made the news.

At the beginning of my third year, workers came into my unit to paint the common area and vacant rooms for the upcoming school year. They left debris and paint residue on the floors, pulled out the couch and stove from the wall, left FOOTPRINTS on the table and coutners, and  left open bottles and supplies in the hall. Since they didn't finish in one day, I assumed they would clean up once they were done, but they never did. I ended up having to clean the mess myself, and I documented the entire experience. While I was irritated, I was not at all surprised.

If I had to finish my final years at Howard again, I would NOT choose Vie Towers.

title: Vie Towers
name: Josh Veasy
text:
First year was great — second year is off to a rough start

I had a really solid first year living at Vie Towers. My apartment was on a higher floor, clean, and had good privacy. That experience was honestly great, and it’s the only reason I’m giving this two stars instead of one.

After renewing my lease, I was told I’d be transferred to a different unit due to "operational needs." While I was notified in advance, the change still felt sudden and disappointing — especially since I was not given any choice in the matter despite renewing my lease under the impression I’d stay where I was.

When I moved into the new unit, I was immediately met with issues:

The couch was torn and worn down.

There was rust on the vents and fire alarm.

The toilet had green buildup around the flush button.

And worst of all, the hallway had a funky odor that hits you before you even reach your room.

To top it off, this new unit is on a low floor facing a public walkway, so it feels exposed and lacks any real privacy — a huge downgrade from my previous living situation.

Even though I renewed my lease, my rent still increased, and all I got for the forced move was a one-time $200 concession for August. That doesn’t come close to balancing out the downgrade in quality or privacy.

I’ve tried emailing and calling management multiple times, but they often only respond when and if they feel like it. Communication is slow and inconsistent, which just adds to the stress of situations like this.

If you’re thinking about living here, know that your first experience might not reflect your next, even if you renew. Don’t assume consistency.

EDIT: After management responded to my review asking me to email them, I did — using the exact email address they provided. They still never responded. That just reinforces how inconsistent and dismissive the communication has been. If they’re not going to follow through when they ask you to reach out, it’s hard to trust they’ll follow through on anything else.

Adding to the long list of frustrations, the building's Wi-Fi has now been completely non-functional for over 9 consecutive days. I was told by management on July 15th that a repair would be completed and service restored by the end of July 16th. However, it is now the 17th and the Wi-Fi is still completely down.

To make matters worse, upon calling Single Digits directly, I was informed that the reason for this ongoing delay and missed repair is because Vie Towers management has not responded to their request to come in, further delaying the fix. This directly contradicts the communication I received from management.

This is yet another broken promise and a perfect example of the inconsistent communication, poor follow-through, and apparent internal disorganization I've experienced. Despite paying increased rent, an essential amenity has been unavailable for over a week and a half, with no offer of compensation or rent reduction for this significant inconvenience. This ongoing issue highlights the decline in quality and service, making the overall experience here incredibly disappointing.

text: I enjoy staying in Vie. As a student who attends university in DC, the shuttle service is very accommodating, and the drive is not too bad, depending on how people wanna drive that day lol. The people are very nice, during the semester every time I went downstairs I can’t remember a time they didn’t say hello. The shopping center being right across from Vie is very convenient and I take advantage of that walk almost 2 to 3 times a week. I would definitely recommend a student living here!

title: Vie Towers
name: Evan Lynch
text:
I left a 1-Star review a long time ago but looks like it was removed. So now I’m leaving another one so that others don’t fall into the trap I did.

Lived here in 2022-2023 and it was AWFUL. They will look to charge you for anything possible. I was able to sublease and they tried to charge me for damage on the walls even though scuff marks are classified as “Ordinary Wear and Tear” under Maryland law. Melanie tried to fight me and gaslight me on the issue, but she couldn’t do anything in the end due to the law.

If you’re about to leave this place, I suggest fighting every charge possible citing Maryland Law. It’s all a sham. They are PREDATORY!

Whatever you do, DO NOT sign a lease here.

Edit: Bumping this is up so people can see this

title: Vie Towers
name: Shayla Muse
text: I’ve been living at Vie Towers for about two years now and I honestly love it here. The amenities are some of my favorite things about the building. The rooftop lounge, the rooftop pool, and especially the gym all make the community feel comfortable and enjoyable. Everything is well maintained and convenient, and I’ve never really had anything to complain about during my time here. Overall, Vie Towers has been a great place to live and I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a positive living experience.

title: Vie Towers
name: Jara Jackson
text: This is my first year as a grad student, and I moved here from North Carolina. Vie Towers has been a great place to find community and feel at home. The apartments are clean and furnished, the location is convenient, and the amenities like the gym, access to a free shuttle service to Howard’s Campus, and rooftop lounge are really nice. The staff is friendly and helpful, too. I’d definitely recommend it to other students!
